purpose: Brompheniramine helps relieve allergy symptoms like a runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy throat or skin. It is also used to help with cold symptoms and hay fever. It can help reduce symptoms caused by allergic reactions.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it reacts to something you are allergic to, and histamine is what causes those uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Brompheniramine works by blocking histamine from attaching to certain spots in your body, which helps stop or reduce those symptoms. Think of it like putting a lock on the door so histamine cannot get in and cause trouble.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, so be careful driving or using heavy machinery. You may also notice a dry mouth, dry nose, or dry eyes. Some people feel dizzy, have a headache, upset stomach, or feel a little restless or nervous.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine because it can make the drowsiness much worse. Be careful if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, breathing problems like asthma, or thyroid issues — talk to your doctor first. This medicine is generally not recommended for children under 6 years old without a doctor's guidance. Let your doctor know all other medicines you are taking to avoid interactions.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 and older, the typical dose is 4 mg every 4 to 6 hours, but do not take more than 24 mg in one day. For children 6 to 12 years old, the usual dose is 2 mg every 4 to 6 hours, not more than 12 mg per day. Always follow the instructions on the package or what your doctor tells you, since doses can vary by product.
